span.p:
four fixed slots laid out inline —
no per-instance dict at all

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
__dict__ — a hash table
per object, with resize headroom

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
self.key reads identically in both —
the difference is what sits behind the attribute

div.style: color: rgb(77, 45, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
attribute access becomes a fixed offset instead of a hash
lookup, and each object drops the dict's overhead.
It only matters in the millions — B3 makes one _Node per entry.

div.style: color: rgb(77, 45, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the trade: no new attributes at runtime,
and no __dict__ to poke at while debugging
